newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals jump after U.S. GDP data.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals jump after U.S. GDP data.

text.p: COMEX gold and silver futures jumped sharply early Wednesday after U.S. first quarter GDP rose 5.6 percent, against expectations for a 4.1 percent rise and the implicit price deflator rose 2.3 percent versus expectations for a 1.7 percent rise.

"Fears of inflation were revived a little, overiding fears of more interest rate hikes, plus shortcovering was prompted by the fact that gold again found support its four year lows this week," North American Equity Services COMEX floor trader John Geraghty said.

Precious metals prices firmed Tuesday also after better than expected U.S. data on wage inflation Tuesday, helped U.S. treasury bonds rally sharply, taking some of the pressure off precious metals which are not interest bearing assets.
* COMEX June gold was up $1.10 an ounce at $342.70 an ounce after the first half hour of trade, after trading a $341.50-343.20 early range.
* In the bullion market spot gold was quoted $340.70/20, compared to the London Wednesday morning fix at $340.45 and the New York close Tuesday around $339.70/20.
* COMEX July silver was up 5.5 cents at $472.50 an ounce, after seeing a $4.670-4.740 early range.
* In London Tuesday, spot silver fixed at $4.6425, its lowest in two years, following the slide COMEX July silver to a new contract low at $4.630 on Monday.

* NYMEX July platinum was up 90 cents at $374.50, while NYMEX June palladium was down $1.50 at $156.00, as implied lease rates for palladium in the physical market slipped back from Tuesday's 15 percent.
